writeup.headline: Bloom Energy rates Hold: explosive growth and net cash offset by a very high valuation and weak cash quality.
writeup.thesis: Bloom Energy scores 47, a Hold that sits just 3 points above the Sell line. Growth is the standout, with TTM revenue growth of 112.2% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 139.8% year on year, though growth slowed by 27.9 pp from the previous quarter, and the balance sheet is strong with net cash. Against that, quality scores only 28: once customer prepayments are stripped out the FCF margin is -4.4% (reported 11.5%), and the diluted share count is up 38.0% year on year. Valuation scores 4. In absolute terms the multiples are high, with P/S of 17.7x, EV/EBIT of 118.8x and an FCF yield 5.2 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and the stock is expensive against its own history (P/FCF and EV/EBIT not comparable). The trend score of 40 reflects the price 34.0% below its 52-week high and shares 29.9 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days, while the news score of 68 is helped by a third guidance raise this year to $4.4–4.6 billion.
key_risks: Valuation is high in absolute terms (P/S 17.7x, EV/EBIT 118.8x) and leaves little room for disappointment.
Cash flow leans on customer prepayments: contract liabilities rose $666.1M, and FCF ex-prepayments is negative.
Heavy dilution, with the diluted share count up 38.0% year on year.
Growth is decelerating, slowing by 27.9 pp from the previous quarter.
A pending securities class action over Chinese-sourced scandium remains unresolved.
what_would_change: A drop of just 3 points would push the score below 45 and the rating to Sell, for example through weaker trend or news scores or a further fall in quality.
Moving up 18 points to Buy would likely need a much lower valuation or positive free cash flow without relying on prepayments, which would lift the quality and valuation scores.
A recovery in price strength against SPY and QQQ would improve the trend score of 40.
A sharper slowdown in revenue growth, or a cut to guidance, would weaken the growth and news scores.
